games.title: Dr. Mario
games.note: Mario as a doctor, clearing viruses by matching colours with falling two-part pills.

games.title: Columns
games.note: Jay Geertsen wrote it at Hewlett-Packard in 1989 to learn X11 programming; Sega released it in arcades and on Mega Drive in 1990.

games.title: Puyo Puyo
games.note: First released for MSX2 and the Famicom Disk System; chain reactions drop garbage blobs on your rival.

games.title: Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine
games.note: A Western reskin of Puyo Puyo with characters from the Sonic cartoons.

games.title: Panel de Pon
games.note: Released in the West in 1996 as Tetris Attack, with Yoshi characters and no Tetris gameplay.

games.title: Pokémon Puzzle League
games.note: Panel de Pon's rules with characters from the Pokémon anime, made by Nintendo's American studio.

games.title: Puzzle Bobble
games.note: Called Bust-a-Move in North America; Bub and Bob from Bubble Bobble aim bubbles from a launcher.

games.title: Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo
games.note: Tiny Street Fighter and Darkstalkers characters battle as you smash coloured gems.

games.title: Puzz Loop
games.note: Shoot coloured balls into a chain rolling along a track before it reaches the end.

games.title: Zuma
games.note: A stone frog idol spits balls at chains rolling toward a skull in Aztec-style temples.

games.title: Shariki
games.note: A Russian DOS game and the earliest known match-three: swap neighbouring balls to line up three.

games.title: Bejeweled
games.note: First released online as Diamond Mine; it was PopCap's first hit and spread to dozens of platforms.

games.title: Zoo Keeper
games.note: A Japanese Flash match-three about catching escaped zoo animals, later a hit on the Nintendo DS.

games.title: Puzzle Quest: Challenge of the Warlords
games.note: Set in the world of Steve Fawkner's Warlords strategy games; every battle is a match-three duel.

games.title: SameGame
games.note: First published as Chain Shot! for Fujitsu FM-7 computers; free versions later spread to almost every platform.

games.title: Bubble Witch Saga
games.note: King's first Saga game: a bubble shooter split into separate levels with goals and limited moves.

games.title: Candy Crush Saga
games.note: Grew from King's 2011 portal game Candy Crush; launched on Facebook in April 2012 and on iPhone that November.

games.title: Pet Rescue Saga
games.note: Tap groups of matching blocks to clear them and bring the pets safely down.

games.title: Farm Heroes Saga
games.note: A farm match-three where each level asks for a set number of fruit and vegetable 'cropsies'.

games.title: Candy Crush Soda Saga
games.note: Soft-launched in May 2014 and released on Facebook that October; soda levels make candies float upward.

games.title: Candy Crush Jelly Saga
games.note: Soft-launched in 2015; levels are about spreading jelly, with boss battles against the Jelly Queen.

games.title: Pyramid Solitaire Saga
games.note: King's take on pyramid solitaire, laid out on an Egyptian-themed adventure map.

games.title: Papa Pear Saga
games.note: King's pachinko-style Saga game, shut down in January 2022.

games.title: Royal Match
games.note: Istanbul studio Dream Games tested it in 2020; you renovate King Robert's castle by beating levels.

games.title: Microsoft Solitaire
games.note: Written by intern Wes Cherry with card art by Susan Kare; Windows 3.0 included it partly to teach drag-and-drop.

games.title: Minesweeper
games.note: First sold in a Windows Entertainment Pack in 1990, then bundled with Windows for over two decades.

games.title: Mined-Out
games.note: A ZX Spectrum game where a detector counts nearby mines as you cross a minefield.

games.title: Lumines
games.note: A PSP launch game where a timeline sweeps the board in time with each music track.

games.title: Rez
games.note: A rail shooter where every shot adds to the music, inspired by the painter Wassily Kandinsky.

games.title: Tetris Effect
games.note: Named after the real effect of seeing falling blocks after playing too long; fully playable in VR.

games.title: Tetris 99
games.note: 99 players compete at once, sending garbage lines at chosen rivals until one is left.

games.title: Hexic
games.note: Tetris creator Pajitnov's game of rotating hexagon clusters; Hexic HD came preinstalled on early Xbox 360 hard drives.

games.title: Threes
games.note: Slide numbered cards to merge 1s and 2s into 3s and their doubles; it took about 14 months to design.
Made in a weekend by a 19-year-old Italian developer and released as free, open-source code.

links.took: Tetris popularized falling-block puzzles; Dr. Mario drops two-coloured pills.
links.added: Viruses already on the board, cleared by lining up four of a colour.

links.took: Tetris popularized the falling-block puzzle; Columns drops three-jewel columns.
links.added: Match three or more jewels in any direction, including diagonals, and cycle their order.
links.extra: Wikipedia places it among the puzzle games that followed Tetris's success; a 1993 review called it 'like Tetris but a bit better'.

links.took: Tetris popularized falling-block puzzles and head-to-head versions of them.
links.added: Blobs that pop in groups of four, chain reactions and garbage sent to your rival.

links.took: Matching falling pieces by colour, building on Dr. Mario's mechanics.
links.added: Chain reactions and versus battles against cartoon opponents.

links.took: Puyo Puyo's exact rules and versus play, reskinned by Compile.
links.added: Sonic cartoon villains and Dr. Robotnik as the final opponent.

src.t: Wikipedia: Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine

links.took: Puyo Puyo popularized versus puzzle battles where chains bury your rival in garbage.
links.added: Crash gems, power gems and Street Fighter characters who fight as you play.

links.took: Colour matching with falling pairs, building on Dr. Mario's mechanics.
links.added: Big power gems, counter gems and chibi fighters reacting to every combo.

links.took: Columns started a line of puzzle games about shifting and swapping pieces.
links.added: Blocks rise from below, and you swap pairs side to side to set off chains.
links.extra: The genre history credits Panel de Pon with introducing the tile-swapping mechanic Bejeweled later popularized.

links.took: Panel de Pon's swap-and-rise rules, kept intact.
links.added: Pokémon anime characters and a 3D mode on a spinning cylinder.

links.took: Clearing coloured pieces by grouping them, which the genre history says influenced it.
links.added: Aiming and bouncing bubbles off walls instead of dropping them.

links.took: Bub and Bob, the bubble dragons, and Bubble Bobble's music and style.
links.added: A puzzle spin-off: fire bubbles from a launcher to match three colours.

links.took: Firing coloured balls from a launcher to match three.
links.added: The balls roll along a track as a chain heading for a hole.

links.took: Shooting coloured balls to match three or more.
links.added: Rolling chains, Aztec temples and a frog idol that spins to aim.

links.took: Shooting balls into a chain that rolls along a track toward an exit.
links.added: Power-up balls, a frog shooter and release on PCs and the web.
links.extra: Mitchell said Zuma infringed on Puzz Loop; PopCap replied that it was 'not an exact clone'.

links.took: PopCap's casual design: quick to learn, bright feedback, sold as a download.
links.added: Rolling chains and aiming instead of swapping gems.

links.took: Swapping neighbouring pieces to line up three, from the first match-three game.
links.added: Gems, cascading combos and an untimed mode, first sold online as Diamond Mine.
links.extra: The genre history says Shariki 'led directly to' Bejeweled.

links.took: Bejeweled's swap-to-match-three on a grid, against the clock.
links.added: Cute animal tiles and a race to meet a quota of each animal.

links.took: Bejeweled-style gem swapping on an 8x8 board.
links.added: RPG battles: matches deal damage, earn mana and power spells against an opponent.
links.extra: The genre history says it led to many games that use tile matching as a battle system.

links.took: Swap-to-match-three, via King's portal game Miner Speed, which borrowed from Bejeweled.
links.added: Hundreds of short levels with goals, move limits and special candies.
links.extra: Wikipedia's genre history calls it King's 'Bejeweled clone' that 'established a new type of tile-matching game'.

links.took: Puzzle Bobble's bubble shooting; the genre history calls it a Puzzle Bobble clone.
links.added: Separate levels with goals and move limits on a map, played with Facebook friends.

links.took: King's saga structure from Bubble Witch Saga: levels with goals and limited moves on a map.
links.added: Match-three candies on Miner Speed's cross-platform tech, syncing progress between Facebook and phones.
links.extra: King co-founder Sebastian Knutsson proposed the saga map, made to look like a board game.

links.took: King's saga format: a map of short levels, lives and goals.
links.added: Tap groups of matching blocks to clear them and drop pets to safety.

links.took: SameGame popularized clearing a board by tapping groups of matching blocks.
links.added: Pets to rescue, level goals, boosters and King's saga map.

links.took: Candy Crush Saga's match-three levels, lives and saga map.
links.added: Collect quotas of specific crops instead of clearing jelly or ingredients.

links.took: Candy Crush's candies, characters and level structure.
links.added: Soda levels where candies float upward, plus new candy types.

links.took: Candy Crush's candies and saga map.
links.added: Spreading jelly across the board, with boss levels against the Jelly Queen.

links.took: Match-three levels with goals and move limits, the template Candy Crush made standard.
links.added: Faster animations, stronger boosters and a castle you renovate between levels.
links.extra: Reviewers also compared its speed and feel to Peak Games' Toon Blast.

links.took: Swapping pieces to match three, the core Wikipedia says it shares with Bejeweled.
links.added: A free-to-play castle story starring King Robert.

links.took: King's saga map of levels, lives and goals.
links.added: Pyramid solitaire hands instead of a bubble shooter.

links.took: Microsoft Solitaire popularized solitaire as a computer game.
links.added: Pyramid rules, level goals and an Egyptian map to travel.

links.took: King's saga format: levels, lives and boosters.
links.added: Pachinko-style shots that bounce through pegs.

links.took: Peggle popularized aiming a ball to bounce through and clear pegs.
links.added: King's saga levels, lives and boosters.

links.took: Crossing a minefield using a count of nearby mines.
links.added: A grid you uncover by clicking, with flags to mark suspected mines.
links.extra: Eurogamer credits Mined-Out as the inspiration; co-author Curt Johnson says Microsoft borrowed from a different game.

links.took: Tetris popularized falling-block puzzles; Lumines drops 2x2 blocks of two colours.
links.added: A timeline sweeping in rhythm with the music clears same-coloured squares.

links.took: Tetsuya Mizuguchi's idea of play and music blending into one experience.
links.added: Applied it to a block puzzle on Sony's new handheld.

links.took: Mizuguchi's music-reactive puzzle design from Lumines.
links.added: Official Tetris rules, a Zone mode that freezes time and full VR support.

links.took: Mizuguchi's synesthesia: sound, light and rumble reacting to every move.
links.added: Brought it to Tetris, with stages that shift from oceans to deserts to space.

links.took: Tetris itself, with official modern rules.
links.added: Music, visuals and sound that react to every move.

links.took: Tetris's official pieces and rules.
links.added: 99 players at once, with attacks you aim at rivals.

links.took: PUBG popularized the battle royale: many players, one survivor.
links.added: Turned it into Tetris, with garbage lines as weapons.

links.took: Alexey Pajitnov, Tetris's creator, designed it.
links.added: Rotate clusters of hexagons to match colours instead of dropping pieces.

links.took: Sliding tiles to merge matching numbers, the format Threes made popular.
links.added: Free, open-source and simpler: double numbers until you reach 2048.
links.extra: The genre history says merge games got a boost from Threes' success.
